criteria.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/introspect.rs builds a failed check whose output_tail has a cargo `failures:` section with a panic line, then CI cleanup lines (post-job cleanup and a Node.js 20 warning), and whose failed_tests is non-empty. It asserts the rendered input names each failed test and its panic line and contains no cleanup lines. Run `cargo test -p athena-core introspect`.
criteria.evidence: The test a_failed_check_names_its_failed_tests_and_panic_without_cleanup_lines builds a tail with a `failures:` section and a panic line, then 'Post job cleanup.', a git command line and a Node.js 20 warning. It sets failed_tests to two names, one of which (widget::other) is not in the tail. It asserts that both names and both panic lines are present and that 'Post job cleanup', 'Node.js 20' and '/usr/bin/git' are absent. It passed when I ran it. Reading the base code, it would fail without the change: the base printed no failed_tests, so widget::other would be missing, and the base clip_tail kept the whole tail of about 330 characters, cleanup lines included.

criteria.criterion: A new unit test shows a failed check with empty failed_tests and plain output still renders its tail, clipped to TAIL_CAP. Run `cargo test -p athena-core introspect`.
criteria.evidence: The test a_failed_check_without_failed_tests_still_shows_its_clipped_tail uses a tail of 1200 'z' characters followed by 'plain end'. It asserts the input contains 'plain end', has no 'failed tests:' label and has no run of more than TAIL_CAP 'z' characters. It passed.

criteria.criterion: The failed-check loop in introspect.rs no longer passes the raw output_tail to clip_tail alone. It prints the failed_tests names and builds the excerpt from the `failures:` section, or from the text before the cleanup lines. A diff line shows this.
criteria.evidence: In the diff, failure_details changes `clip_tail(&c.output_tail, TAIL_CAP)` to `failure_excerpt(&c.output_tail)` and adds the prefix `failed tests: {names}; `, capped at DETAIL_CAP names with a '(+N more)' count. The new function failure_excerpt (introspect.rs:966-983) cuts the text at the first cleanup-marker line. When a `failures:` line is present it takes the text from there, clipped to TAIL_CAP; otherwise it falls back to clip_tail.

criteria.criterion: The existing introspect tests pass, including the one at ~3042 that checks the tail is clipped to TAIL_CAP. Run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: All 38 introspect-filtered tests pass in my targeted run, including counts_and_text_are_capped (the TAIL_CAP clip test, now at about line 3080) and a_failed_check_is_listed_apart_and_is_not_an_unmet_criterion. findings.summary: The second cleanup marker, 'node.js 20 actions are deprecated', does not match the runner's real warning text, so it never fires on stored data.
findings.evidence: In the evidence snapshot, 9 verification.json files contain 'Node.js 20 is deprecated' and none contain 'Node.js 20 actions are deprecated'. The new test uses the made-up form. It does no harm in practice: every stored tail with the warning also has 'Post job cleanup', which comes earlier and ends the body. Matching on 'node.js 20 is deprecated', or on the '##[warning]Node.js' prefix, would match the real text.

findings.summary: The module doc still says the input shows 'the end of its output tail' for each failed check.
findings.evidence: Lines 22-24 of the module doc describe each failed check by its name and the end of its output tail. The input now also gives the failed_tests names, and the excerpt is the `failures:` section or the text before the cleanup lines.

findings.summary: When the start of a `failures:` section was cut off the stored tail, the excerpt holds only the name list, without the panic text.
findings.evidence: failure_excerpt takes the first line that reads exactly 'failures:'. If the stored tail starts after the panic block, that first match is the second, names-only `failures:` list. The panic text is then not in the tail at all, so nothing better was available, and the failed_tests names are still printed.

summary: The change works: I recommend a pass. Each failed check in the introspection input now lists its failed_tests names. Its excerpt is now the cargo `failures:` section, or, if there is none, the text before the CI runner's post-job cleanup lines, instead of the raw last 600 characters. When there are no cleanup lines and no `failures:` section, the old tail clip still applies. Two new tests pass when I run them: one checks the test names, the panic lines and that no cleanup lines appear; the other checks that a plain tail is still clipped to TAIL_CAP. Reading the base code, the first test would fail without the change. I checked the logic against the real verification.json files for vdtn and h7de in the evidence snapshot. For vdtn the excerpt starts at `failures:` and includes the panic from xtask/src/main.rs:850. For h7de the failing test's output was cut off before the stored tail began, so the excerpt is the last 600 characters before 'Post job cleanup.', and the failed_tests list still names the test. fmt, clippy and the full test run passed in Athena's recorded CI checks. Only the two expected files changed. One minor issue: the 'node.js 20 actions are deprecated' marker does not match the real warning ('Node.js 20 is deprecated'). It has no effect in practice, because 'Post job cleanup' always comes first in the stored data. Two nits: the module doc's description of the input is stale, and the excerpt is limited when the start of a `failures:` section was cut off.
